title: How Our Reporters Navigate Politics at Thanksgiving
summary: A holiday gathering can be joyous. And fraught. Here’s how six reporters deal with their own dinner-table discourse. (And when they switch the topic to serving spoons or animal sex.)
authors: Megan DiTrolio, Michael Barbaro, Vanessa Friedman, Ruth Graham, Erica L. Green, Yair Rosenberg and Kim Severson

title: Border Barrier Cannot be Removed for Decades, Texas Republicans and D.O.J. Agree
summary: Just before Democrats take over the state government, Trump administration and outgoing Republican officials in Texas ink legal settlement barring removal of wire for 30 years.
caption: Razor wire along the Rio Grande in Eagle Pass, Tex., in 2021.

title: Trump Rejoiced in the Market’s Nvidia Surge. It Didn’t Last Long.
summary: The retreat of the stock market in recent days shows how President Trump’s push to reinstall the company’s chief executive has collided with the realities of his other policies.
caption: President Trump has made it clear that he does not subscribe to the theory that if a president is responsible for market surges, he must also be responsible for declines.

title: Bipartisan Desire to Regulate A.I. Faces Obstacles in Congress
summary: Members of both parties say they want to tackle artificial intelligence policy, but the slow pace of legislating and turf battles could stand in the way.
caption: Lawmakers’ growing focus on A.I. comes after a year of startling milestones and a midterm election cycle punctuated by a voter backlash to the technology.

title: Trump Administration’s Cuts to SNAP Threaten Free School Meals
summary: The Trump administration’s cuts and proposed regulatory changes to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program would have consequences for school lunch and breakfast.
caption: Last year’s sweeping domestic policy bill pushed an estimated two million children off food stamps, and even more may stop receiving free school lunch next year as parts of the tax cut law take effect.

title: Strobe Talbott, Journalist Who Joined Clinton’s State Department, Has Died
summary: He was a reporter and foreign affairs columnist at Time and then served as deputy secretary of state and president of the Brookings Institution. He was 80.
caption: Strobe Talbott, who lived with Bill Clinton when they were Rhodes scholars at Oxford, helped negotiate an end to the war in Kosovo during Mr. Clinton’s second term as president.

title: Thanksgiving Is Back on the Menu for Francesca Hong, the Failed Wisconsin Governor Candidate
summary: Francesca Hong, who took heat over a social media post condemning the holiday during her run for the Democratic nomination, now has regrets — and is laughing it all off.
caption: Francesca Hong, who ran for the Democratic nomination for Wisconsin governor this year, faced criticism for a six-year-old social media post that called for Thanksgiving to be canceled.

title: How a Thanksgiving Tradition Connects to Presidential Powers
summary: As President Trump pardons turkeys for Thanksgiving, our chief White House correspondent Peter Baker takes a look back at the history of the tradition and the presidential power of the pardon.
authors: Peter Baker, Gilad Thaler, Brian Oh, Pierre Kattar and Shawn Paik
